mechanistic_claim_tested: Beta-cell secretory defect precedes/exceeds insulin resistance in FA children
key_finding: 46% of 39 FA children had abnormal glucose metabolism; insulinogenic index reduced (FA-AGM 44 vs REF 173 pM/mM) and disposition index reduced, while HOMA-IR unchanged
disease_subtype_context: Pediatric FA, mostly pre-transplant, no prior diabetes dx
limitations: Cross-sectional; OGTT surrogate indices not IVGTT/clamp; younger FA vs older REF controls; no genotype/beta-cell-mass data

mechanistic_claim_tested: FA-pathway (FANCC) loss causes cell-autonomous beta-cell oxidative-stress apoptosis and lowers insulin/glucokinase
key_finding: siRNA FANCC knockdown abolished protection vs oxidative-stress apoptosis; FANCC overexpression protective; insulin and glucokinase mRNA decreased
limitations: Single immortalized cell line; cytoplasmic anti-apoptotic FANCC role partly DNA-repair-independent; no p53 readout; no in vivo mass/first-phase data

mechanistic_claim_tested: Endogenous DNA damage -> p53/p21 -> beta-cell senescence & reduced islet mass -> diabetes
key_finding: NHEJ-deficient p53R172P mice accumulate DNA damage, upregulate p53/p21, lose beta-cell proliferation, develop senescence, reduced islet mass, severe diabetes at 3-5 mo
limitations: Different repair pathway (NHEJ) than FA (ICL); phenotype is senescence not apoptosis; not FA genes

mechanistic_claim_tested: Oxidative stress activates p53 in beta cells
key_finding: H2O2 stabilizes p53 and activates PARP in pancreatic beta cells; ROS/RNS induce DNA damage and reduce viability

mechanistic_claim_tested: Genotoxic/crosslinking agents impair GSIS and induce beta-cell apoptosis
key_finding: Doxorubicin (topo II/crosslinker) impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and viability; induced caspase-3/7 and p53-linked apoptosis
disease_subtype_context: INS-1 beta cells and mouse islets
limitations: Pharmacologic genotoxin, not FA genetic model

mechanistic_claim_tested: Primary lesion is ROS-driven peripheral insulin resistance
disease_subtype_context: Fanca-/Fancc-deficient mice: hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, weight gain on HFD; reduced IR tyrosine phosphorylation, increased IRS-1 serine phosphorylation; Quercetin rescues
confidence: FA mouse models (Fanca, Fancc), HFD challenge
column9: Diet-dependent; does not measure first-phase secretion or beta-cell mass; hyperinsulinemia argues against pure secretory failure

mechanistic_claim_tested: Endocrine survey of FA quantifies glucose/insulin abnormalities
key_finding: Hyperinsulinemia in 28/39 (72%), impaired glucose tolerance 25%, overt diabetes present; broad endocrinopathy (81%)
limitations: Hyperinsulinemia suggests insulin resistance component; heterogeneous ages; older cohort methods

mechanistic_claim_tested: Adult FA glucose phenotype and transplant context
key_finding: Diabetes 10%, hypothyroidism 42%, low BMI 31% in 52 adults; 69% had HSCT
limitations: Retrospective single-center; transplant confounds adult diabetes attribution

mechanistic_claim_tested: Endocrine screening consensus recognizing abnormal glucose/insulin metabolism in FA
key_finding: ~80% of FA have >=1 endocrine abnormality incl. abnormal glucose/insulin metabolism; screening recommended
Stable-isotope study: compromised glucose oxidation, enhanced ketogenesis, metabolic inflexibility
limitations: Abstract truncated; systemic not beta-cell-specific; supports metabolic vulnerability context

mechanistic_claim_tested: HSCT/TBI causes early insulin resistance independent of FA
key_finding: 7/45 (15.6%) non-obese pediatric HSCT survivors had abnormal glucose tolerance with central fat redistribution; TBI associated
limitations: Non-FA cohort; establishes transplant as alternative cause of later glucose abnormality

mechanistic_claim_tested: TBI-based HSCT drives insulin resistance in survivors
key_finding: 5/10 young adults post-HSCT+TBI had insulin resistance; abdominal obesity in all
limitations: Small pilot; non-FA; relevant to adult-diabetes attribution
